verses.text: By the dawn.
By the ten nights.
By the even and the odd.
By the night as it passes—
is there in that a sworn oath for whoever has a mind[1]?
Have you sg not seen what your Lord did to Ād[2] —
Iram, (the city) of the pillars
whose like has never been created in the lands;
and Thamûd[3], who carved the rocks in the valley;
and Pharaoh of the stakes?
They (all) exceeded all limits in the lands
and spread much corruption therein,
so your sg Lord poured down upon them a scourge of punishment;
indeed, your Lord is certainly ever-watchful.
So, as for man, whenever his Lord tries him through honoring and blessing him, he says, “My Lord has honored me.”
But whenever He tries him through restricting [4] his provision, he says, “My Lord has insulted me.”
But no! Rather, you pl do not honor [5] the orphan,
and you do not urge one another [6] to (serve) food to the destitute sg,
and you devour inheritance (of the vulnerable) greedily,
and you love wealth immensely.
But no! When the earth is pounded to dust, pounding after pounding;
and your sg Lord comes with the angels, rank after rank;
and on that day, Hell is made to come forward—on that day man reminds himself, but how will reminding avail him?
He says, “If only I had put forth something (good) for my life.”
On that day, none can punish as He punishes [7],
and none can shackle as He shackles.
O you tranquil self,
return to your Lord, well pleased and well pleasing;
so enter among My servants,
and enter My Garden.

footnotes.2: The pagan tribe of Prophet Hûd.
footnotes.3: The pagan tribe of Prophet Salih.
footnotes.4: Qira’at: Ibn ‘Amer and Abu Ja’far read it as: “…through utterly restricting his provision,”
footnotes.5: Qira’at: Abu ‘Amr and Ya’qub read it as: “Rather, they do not honor the orphan, 18 18 and they do not urge (others) to (serve) food to the destitute sg, 19 19 and they devour inheritance (of the vulnerable) greedily, 20 20 and they love wealth immensely.”
footnotes.6: Qira’at: Nafie’, Ibn Kathir and Ibn ‘Amer read it as: “…and you do not urge (others) to (serve) food…”
footnotes.7: Qira’at: Al-Kesa’i and Ya’qub read it as: “On that day, none is punished as he is punished, 26 26 and none is shackled as he is shackled.”
